summary: Learn GS1 identifiers, EPCIS event mapping, and traceability KPIs in five days. Review the supply chain visibility course outline.
lede: Supply chain track and trace connects product identifiers with movement events so teams can reconstruct histories and find record gaps. For logistics coordinators, quality specialists, and supply chain analysts, the course builds practical skills in mapping traceability chains, checking GTIN, SSCC, and GLN identifiers, and investigating missing or conflicting records using GS1 standards and EPCIS 2.0. It also introduces event sharing, capture options, and visibility measures.
audienceIntro: This course is for professionals who create, maintain, analyse, or use traceability records across supply chain operations. It suits foundation-level learners who need practical methods for connecting product identifiers, movement events, and exception reporting.
modules: GS1 Digital Link and Partner Exchange
prerequisites: Prior supply chain experience is useful but not required. No coding or programming is required. Bring a working knowledge of your organization’s basic product, shipment, or supplier processes if available; advanced digital topics are covered at conceptual or operational-awareness level.
